title: A fast and non-invasive artificial intelligence olfactory-like system that aids diagnosis of Parkinson's disease
summary: Three learned classifiers were evaluated on sebum VOC data from Parkinson’s patients and controls; the best separated these groups but did not predict disease progression. Clinical diagnoses under UK Brain Bank criteria and matched controls provide the reference; held-out test split and repeated sensor runs are reported. Authors disclose no GC-MS verification of identities, possible medication/sample-volume confounding, and need for larger rigorous studies; no severity result.
ai_technology: GBDT, random forest and XGBoost classifiers operate on measured skin-sebum VOC time-series to distinguish clinically diagnosed PD from matched healthy controls; this is the enabled diagnostic result.
organization: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University Medical College

evidence.tested: Methods report 121 PD and 129 controls split 80:20 (200 train, 50 test); held-out GBDT sensitivity 83.33%, specificity 84%, AUC 0.893. Severity prediction failed, so scope is cross-sectional case-control discrimination.
